name: devtools-close-while-docked
description: Phase C2 (partial): closing DevTools while it is docked must detach cleanly and never crash. Cmd+Opt+I opens the dock, a second Cmd+Opt+I closes it, and the pane must report docked=0 - the path that runs ClearDevToolsFocusTracker + RestoreDevToolsFocus + SetWebContents(nullptr), which is where a teardown UAF would surface. The final Cmd+Q is the liveness check: a process that already crashed cannot quit on command, so a passing quit assertion proves the app survived the undock. Does NOT cover the ASAN window-close case or tab-close-while-docked - those need an ASAN build and are still open.

actions.note: let the space and its single tab render
make Atrium frontmost before any synthetic key
let the DevTools frontend load and dock
toggle DevTools back off - the undock/teardown path under test
let the detach + focus restore settle

assertions.label: devtools-docked
assertions.note: it actually docked first - without this the undock assertion below would pass vacuously

assertions.label: devtools-undocked
assertions.note: The pane detached its DevTools WebContents on close
assertions.desc: the undock must come AFTER a dock. Atrium logs 'devtools pane ... docked=0 bounds=0,0 0x0 hide_inspected=0' at LAUNCH, and the line it logs after a real undock is byte-identical - same pane pointer, same zero bounds - so presence alone was true of an app that never opened DevTools. This assertion once passed while DevTools was completely dead. Ordering is the only thing that separates them.

assertions.note: liveness: a process that crashed during the undock teardown has no window to report. Deliberately NOT a Cmd+Q quit probe - a dropped Cmd+Q would read as a FAILED assertion even though the process being alive is exactly what this is trying to prove, so quit inverts the signal here.
